title: Clean Slate: Component decomposition, portability checklist, and diffable publish preview
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
The current Figma library has accumulated a number of large compound components (complex card, action-row, data-table rows) with multiple overlapping variant axes and inconsistent auto-layout constraints. This makes small updates risky, causes noisy publishes, and blocks teams from safely reusing primitives across feature files.

Problem statement:
- Variants are combinatorial and include presentation + state + density axes that should be split into smaller primitives.
- Auto-layout constraints are inconsistent (mix of fixed and hug) leading to position jumps when resizing or when instances are nested.
- Naming and grouping across pages (Primitives / Atoms / Composed) are inconsistent; tokens are scattered between local and library-level styles.
- Publish diffs are noisy; consumers can't easily review what changed before accepting a library update.

Goals:
1) Decompose three target compound components (Button group, Compact data row, Metric card) into explicit primitives and thin composition layers so variants are minimal and predictable.
2) Standardize auto-layout rules for horizontal/vertical stacks and define when to use fixed vs fill vs hug in nested contexts.
3) Create a portability checklist that ensures instances can be copied to product files without layout regressions (token mapping, resizing behavior, text truncation rules).
4) Implement a lightweight "diffable publish preview" flow: pre-publish report showing affected tokens, renamed components, and bounding-box delta heatmap for changed instances.

Success metrics:
- 90% reduction in high-risk variant combinations for the three target components.
- Publish review time reduced by 60% for affected files in the first two releases.
- Less than 2 regressions reported by product teams in the first month post-publish.

Deliverables:
- Figma file: "DS - Decomposed Primitives (WIP)" with PR-ready examples (link below).
- Portability checklist document (Confluence) with verification steps and automated QA items.
- Publish preview spec and prototype plugin script that generates a diff report (CSV + preview layers).
- Migration playbook for maintainers to deprecate old compound variants (gradual removal plan + instance migration steps).

Acceptance criteria:
- Each decomposed component has at most two variant axes (appearance + state) and relies on composition for density/spacing.
- All primitives have documented token dependencies (color, spacing, typography) referenced by name, not local overrides.
- Auto-layout rules documented and applied: stacks use consistent spacing token, nested fills only used when child width is unconstrained.
- Pre-publish diff report runs against the current prod library and highlights no-blocking regressions for at least three example consumer files.

Non-goals:
- Full migration of every component in the library. This ticket targets three compound components as a pattern we can reuse.
- Implementing an enterprise CI for Figma publishes (we'll provide a spec instead).

Stakeholders:

- Design Systems Eng: Mateo Ruiz (plugin / publish tooling)

Artifacts / Links:
- Figma WIP file: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/DS-Decomposed-Primitives-WIP
- Confluence checklist: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/portability-checklist
- GitHub PR (plugin prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-systems/pull/512
- Example consumer file used for QA: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Product-Settings-Mock

Planned tasks (high-level):
1) Audit and document current variant axes and token usage for the three components (2 days).
2) Draft decomposition pattern: primitives, composition layer, example instances (2 days).
3) Apply auto-layout rules and run resizing edge cases in consumer files (1 day).
4) Create portability checklist and confluence page (0.5 day).
5) Prototype publish preview script and generate sample diff reports (1.5 days).
6) Internal review with frontend and product teams; iterate (1 day).
7) Schedule gated publish and notify consumers with migration notes (0.5 day).

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Consumer files with heavy local overrides could break when primitives change. Mitigation: include instance migration notes and a fallback variant strategy (ghost variant that maps old props to new composition).
- Risk: Plugin prototype may not cover complex layout deltas. Mitigation: start with a conservative report (tokens changed, component renames) and add bounding-box delta later.

Notes for implementation:
- Prefer token references instead of local style overrides; add a migration step to convert local fills to library tokens where possible.
- When decomposing buttons, separate icon + label + container as three primitives; keep the compound variant only as a composition example.
- For table/data row, move density into a row container that controls padding, not into cell variant axes.
